headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct write or network pathways, but shared file-based workflows could still misroute content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can use MCP and reads/writes project files like CLAUDE.md, while LlamaFactory has no shared channel or clipboard/filesurface. The pairwise injection path is therefore not default, but if an operator bridges caveman outputs into files that LlamaFactory later consumes, prompt-like content could be misread. Uncertainty is limited by the docs-only profiles.
conditions: IF caveman outputs are copied into a file that LlamaFactory later ingests as instructions
IF an operator enables an MCP bridge or shared workspace between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between outputs and prompts
Review file contents before reusing them as prompts
Use provenance labels on any shared notes
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization between producer and consumer

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, but LlamaFactory has read_filesystem false, write_filesystem false, and no file or API surfaces. That makes direct leakage unlikely in default settings; the main risk is accidental operator transfer of sensitive notes into a channel LlamaFactory can see. No evidence shows either agent exfiltrates data.
conditions: IF sensitive caveman notes are manually copied into a medium LlamaFactory can access
IF a shared filesystem or export path is introduced
mitigations: Store sensitive notes outside shared folders
Avoid copying session logs into downstream prompts
Restrict exports to redacted summaries
Verify LlamaFactory cannot read the caveman workspace
requires-engineering: add access controls on any shared storage

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman has no listed filesystem write, git, or network egress, and LlamaFactory explicitly lacks shell, git, filesystem write, subprocess, and network egress. With no overlapping mutable resource, the pair cannot create a write-write conflict in the documented configuration.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory
IF future versions add shared mutable scopes not present in these profiles
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only relative to shared artifacts
Do not grant shared git or filesystem write access
Run them under separate OS users
Monitor for future capability changes

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman can produce project notes and CLAUDE.md content, but LlamaFactory has no documented action-taking authority and no file or stdin/stdout surfaces. The pair therefore lacks the default A-to-B automation path that would turn one agent's output into irreversible downstream actions; any cascade would require an operator to manually relay content.
conditions: IF an operator feeds caveman-generated text into LlamaFactory without verification
IF LlamaFactory is wrapped by an external workflow that acts on its outputs
mitigations: Require human review before reuse of outputs
Separate drafting from execution roles
Log source provenance for reused text
Use checklists for any downstream action
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action execution

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated-data handling mismatch is documented for either agent. caveman lists generic project-note data classes, while LlamaFactory lists none and has no secrets or OAuth scopes; there is no evidence of a compliance breach pathway in this pair.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data through either agent
IF a jurisdictional or retention policy is added outside these profiles
mitigations: Classify data before use
Avoid placing regulated data in either workflow
Document retention settings if added
Re-review if residency requirements change
